topics.topic: Audit coverage for failed snapshot imports after route checks
questions: Are principal-disablement, storage, and Registry failures after successful route checks audited as snapshot-import attempts?

quotes:
Every significant action records actor provenance: principal (`user_id`,
viewer, or service principal with credential/key version), `project_id`,
action, time, result, and affected business entity.

This includes viewer and
grant management, access revocation, expense changes, progress updates,
payment registration, photo publication/visibility changes, budget changes,
snapshot import (with `estimate_id`, `estimate_version`, `contract_version`,
content fingerprint, rejection reasons), and version activation (with the
human staff actor).

a principal disabled in
between, or a storage or Registry failure during the import (an HTTP 404
from the Registry among them, R6), is answered as that failure and records
nothing: neither an import result nor an audit record.
judgement.divergence: After a post-check principal-disablement, storage failure, or Registry failure, one implementation records a rejected `snapshot.import` audit with actor provenance, while another records no audit; an administrator or auditor notices.
judgement.why: The general audit promise explicitly includes snapshot imports and rejection reasons, while R0-25 explicitly requires no audit record for the named post-check failures.

bases.passage:
Every significant action records actor provenance: principal (`user_id`,
viewer, or service principal with credential/key version), `project_id`,
action, time, result, and affected business entity.

a principal disabled in
between, or a storage or Registry failure during the import (an HTTP 404
from the Registry among them, R6), is answered as that failure and records
nothing: neither an import result nor an audit record.

viewer, or service principal with credential/key version), `project_id`,
action, time, result, and affected business entity.

a principal disabled in
between, or a storage or Registry failure during the import (an HTTP 404
from the Registry among them, R6), is answered as that failure and records
nothing: neither an import result nor an audit record.

witness.initial: An active service principal has a valid bearer credential, project grant, import capability, and an active Registry project.
events: The service principal publishes an approved estimate snapshot and passes the route's access checks.
The principal is disabled, or storage or Registry fails, during the import.
outcomes: The Audit section records actor provenance for the significant snapshot-import action, including its rejection reason.
R0-25 records neither an import result nor an audit record.
basis:
Producer of approved estimate snapshots through the portal-owned inbound
publication contract, authenticated as a `ServicePrincipal`.

Before the import, the import
route checks the producer's access: its authenticated bearer credential, its
scope and grant for the project, its capability, and that the Registry knows
the project as active.

a principal disabled in
between, or a storage or Registry failure during the import (an HTTP 404
from the Registry among them, R6), is answered as that failure and records
nothing: neither an import result nor an audit record.

topics.topic: Import-result classification for post-route-check project, grant, or capability changes
questions: What import-result outcome represents a project becoming nonexistent or inactive, loss of a grant, or refusal of a capability after the route check?

quotes:
`outcome: ImportOutcome (accepted | idempotent_replay |
  integrity_conflict | rejected)`, `reject_reason: ImportRejectReason | None`
  (closed catalog: unsupported_contract_version, currency_mismatch,
  incomplete_content, unknown_project, archived_project, scope_denied,
  invalid_sections) `[closed-choice: reason required iff outcome =
  rejected; None for accepted, idempotent_replay and integrity_conflict]`,

`unknown_project`, `archived_project` and `scope_denied` stay in the
  accepted catalog; the route refuses those cases before the import, so a
  record carries one of them only when access changed between the route's
  check and the import's own (Q20).
judgement.why: State 1 defines one `rejected` import outcome and the exact `unknown_project`, `archived_project`, and `scope_denied` reasons for access changes detected after the route check.

topics.topic: Observable responses for each post-route-check import failure
questions: What observable response does each named post-check failure produce, especially whether principal disablement is concealed and whether Registry HTTP 404 is exposed as not-found or dependency failure?

judgement.why: P2 judged the same API-visible classifications for principal disablement and infrastructure failures against the same changed R0-25 text.

precedent.topic: Define API-visible classifications for failures occurring during import
quotes:
`AuthenticationRejected` and infrastructure failures outside the catalogue
re-raise with nothing written; every business rejection is an answered
record, not an exception.
| `AuthenticationRejected` | `authorization_guard` | 401 |
| `RegistryBoundaryError` | `registry_gateway` | 502 |
| `PersistenceError` | `portal_store` | 500 |
| `BinaryStorageError` | `binary_storage` | 500 |

Any other failure is 500. No failure becomes a success, an empty list or a
  zero.
precedent.why: State 5 maps a disabled principal to the concealed 401 authentication rejection, Registry failures to 502, and storage or otherwise unmapped infrastructure failures to 500, all without an import record.

topics.topic: Precedence when recorded-rejection and no-record failure conditions coincide
questions: Which condition determines the response and persistence result when a recorded-rejection condition and a no-record failure condition both occur during one import?

quotes:
Every project-scoped operation evaluates, in order: valid unexpired
unrevoked session → principal status `active` (and verified email for
staff) → project access (viewer grant / staff assignment semantics / producer
scope) → required capability from R2 → Registry lifecycle policy (R5).
First failure wins; failures are indistinguishable to the caller regarding
account/project existence beyond what their own access already proves.

`capability:snapshot_import.import_snapshot` computes one fingerprint and
   time per attempt and repeats
   `capability:authorization_guard.authorize_snapshot_import` before its
   transaction; only if access changed since step 2 does it classify an
   archived, unknown or scope-denied rejection instead of raising.

Every classified attempt inserts one fresh import record with a fresh
   `import_id` and one `snapshot.import` audit, committed together.

`AuthenticationRejected` and infrastructure failures outside the catalogue
re-raise with nothing written; every business rejection is an answered
record, not an exception.
judgement.why: The later authorization and import flow orders the repeated guard before persistence, makes the first guard failure win, records catalogued business rejections, and lets authentication or infrastructure failures escape with nothing written.

topics.topic: Treatment and persistence of Registry HTTP 404 versus project nonexistence
questions: How is a Registry response saying that the project does not exist distinguished from the explicitly named HTTP 404, and which persistence rule applies when not-existence is represented by HTTP 404?

judgement.why: P1 judged the same distinction between a decoded project-not-existing result and a Registry HTTP 404 against the same changed R0-25 text.

precedent.topic: Classify a Registry 404 during import and determine whether it creates an import result
quotes: | HTTP 404 answer | `not_found` |

Every failed Registry call is answered with exactly one kind of the table and never with a fallback; which transport condition counts as which kind, and the order the gateway tests them in, are the accepted gateway's (notes of `validate_project_reference`, `get_project_context`, `list_active_projects`; `rules.registry_failure_translation`), carried to States 6–7.

- Access refusals of step 2: unknown or ungranted project 404, refused
  capability 403, archived project 409, Registry failure 502; nothing
  recorded (Q20).
precedent.why: State 2 classifies an HTTP 404 response itself as a Registry gateway failure, while a decoded `exists=false` answer is the distinct project-not-existing business result; the former propagates and records no import result.

topics.topic: Viewer visibility when an archived granted project's Registry context is unavailable
questions: When an archived, granted project’s Registry context cannot be obtained, is it omitted from the viewer’s project list or kept visible with read-only access?

quotes:
archiving a Registry project keeps the grant and the project visible
  read-only.

Archived
projects expose the same reads in read-only mode.

The one exception
is the project list: a granted project whose Registry context cannot be
obtained is left out of it rather than listed without context (accepted
Factory change `00ac72f18d9c`, note `list_viewer_projects`; owner
2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted).
judgement.divergence: When Registry context for an archived granted project cannot be obtained, one implementation omits it from the project list, while another keeps the project visible and exposes its read-only reads; the client viewer notices.
judgement.why: The archival promises keep the granted project visible and expose the same reads, while the new project-list exception requires that granted project to be omitted when its Registry context cannot be obtained.

witness.initial: A client viewer has a valid session and an active grant to an archived Registry project.
events: Registry context for the archived project becomes unavailable.
The client viewer requests the assigned-project list.
The client viewer attempts to open the archived project.
outcomes: The project-list exception omits the granted project rather than listing it without context.
The archival promises keep the project visible and expose the same reads in read-only mode.
basis:
An authenticated viewer sees the list of their assigned projects, opens one,
and reads: Registry project context, budget summary with source and ordered
sections, included and excluded confirmed expenses with `Other expenses`
separate, client-visible documents, work progress and completed work value,
payments and work balance, and the chronological photo gallery.

topics.topic: Whether post-route-check failures persist an import result and import ID
questions: Does every attempt that passes the route checks receive a persisted import result and `import_id`, or are the named post-check failures exceptions?

quotes:
Every
attempt that passes these checks is classified — accepted, idempotent replay,
integrity conflict, or a content rejection — and recorded as a fresh
immutable import result with a fresh `import_id`; the import request is
answered with that result, never with the snapshot itself.

a principal disabled in
between, or a storage or Registry failure during the import (an HTTP 404
from the Registry among them, R6), is answered as that failure and records
nothing: neither an import result nor an audit record.
judgement.divergence: After an attempt passes the route checks and then encounters principal disablement, storage failure, or Registry failure, one implementation persists a fresh import result and `import_id`, while another persists nothing; the producer and an administrator inspecting import history notice.
judgement.why: The first passage universally assigns every post-check attempt a fresh persisted result and `import_id`, while the second explicitly denies both for named post-check failures.
